title: Quotienting a finite module by one element lowers the dimension of its support by at most one
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$). For a finite $R$-module $N$ let $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, $N_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\dots\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ ($-\infty$ when $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\emptyset$, i.e. $N=0$; the same definition for any subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in place of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$). Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $f\in\mathfrak m$. Then $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/fM)+1$.
